intro.title: International experience. A concrete grasp of realities.
intro.p1: Covering international news demands far more than gathering information. It requires understanding contexts, identifying actors, building relationships of trust, adapting to environments and rendering realities with precision.

intro.p3: That experience now underpins an expertise that reaches beyond reporting alone: it informs documentary production, organisational communication and the transmission of the craft itself.

hero.title: A career shaped by the field and the international.
hero.subtitle: From the newsroom to the documentary set, from reporting to consulting: one standard has guided every step — understanding the world in order to tell it better.

bio.title: Professional profile
bio.p1: Alexandre Morel is an international journalist, documentary filmmaker and communications professional. His career was built on the frontlines of international news, in contact with demanding political, economic and human realities.
bio.p2: Trained in journalism at a recognised school, he began in the newsroom before dedicating himself to international reporting. Postings and field coverage taught him what no training can replace: how to read a context, build relationships of trust, and work methodically amid uncertainty.
bio.p3: That experience led him naturally to documentary production — bringing in-depth, patiently constructed narratives to the screen. Then to strategic consulting, where organisations find rare value in journalistic methods: clarity, in a saturated environment.
bio.p4: Today, these four dimensions — reporting, documentary, consulting, training — form a coherent whole: one way of approaching information, in the service of those who need to understand and to tell.

vision.title: A professional philosophy
vision.p1: Information is not a neutral raw material: it is constructed, verified, prioritised. The responsibility of the journalist — and more broadly of anyone producing narratives — is to treat that material honestly.
vision.p2: That conviction runs through the entire professional practice: from reporting to consulting, the same standard applies. Understand before asserting. Document before publishing. Listen before concluding.

meta.title: International Journalism
meta.description: Reporting, investigation and the analysis of international contexts: a journalistic practice grounded in the field, verification and a deep understanding of actors.

hero.title: Information treated as a standard.
hero.subtitle: Understanding contexts, identifying actors, verifying facts and rendering realities with precision: international journalism as it should be practised — with method and humility.

positioning.title: A journalist of both field and analysis
positioning.p1: International journalism cannot be reduced to the mechanics of the news cycle. It demands an understanding of the histories, interests and languages that structure every situation. That understanding is what separates information that is relayed from information that is comprehended.
positioning.p2: The practice rests on three pillars: presence in the field, rigour in gathering, and honesty in reporting. Every story is treated as a system — actors, contexts, consequences — not as a sequence of anecdotes.

reporting.title: The field as proof
reporting.p1: A report is judged by what it shows and what it establishes. Priority goes to filmed situations, testimony gathered in conditions of trust, and verified facts — never to the illustration of a pre-written narrative.
reporting.p2: Investigation begins with sourcing: mapping actors, cross-referencing documents, securing sources. It progresses through verifiable steps and acknowledges its limits when evidence is lacking.
practices: A clear distinction between the established, the probable and the uncertain

research.title: A structured collection method
research.p1: Information gathering follows a simple, demanding protocol: start from open sources, confirm through human sources, document every step. Public data — registries, statistics, imagery, archives — is used with critical distance and context.
research.p2: In environments where information is a stake of power, methodological caution is not optional: it conditions both the safety of sources and the reliability of the work delivered.

analysis.title: Understanding international contexts
analysis.p1: Analysis is the natural extension of reporting: putting events in perspective, connecting scales, identifying what structures a situation beyond its immediate news value. It is a work of reading — historical, economic, political — in the service of clarity.
analysis.p2: This analytical capability serves newsrooms and organisations alike: to understand an environment is to be able to decide and communicate with accuracy.

approach.title: Filming starts with understanding
approach.p1: A quality audiovisual production begins long before the first frame. It starts with research and encounters that determine the angle, the protagonists and the structure of the narrative.
approach.p2: On set, priority goes to real situations and natural light. In post-production, to an edit that respects the time of the people filmed. The result: works that inform, move and endure.

hero.subtitle: The methods of journalism — prioritise, verify, tell — applied to the communications challenges of companies, institutions and NGOs.

value.title: A value proposition born in the field
value.p1: Journalistic experience brings a particular understanding of communications challenges: knowing how to listen, identifying what matters, understanding audiences and turning complex information into clear messages.
value.p2: Where institutional communication locks itself into its own codes, the editorial approach starts from reality: what the organisation does, what its audiences experience, what deserves to be told — and what does not.
value.p3: The ambition: to design content and communications approaches that combine editorial depth, strategic relevance and an understanding of the ground.

editorial.title: Deciding what deserves to be said
editorial.p1: Editorial advisory starts with a diagnosis: what are your real messages, which ones resonate, which ones remain unheard? The journalistic approach — prioritise, document, choose an angle — puts the editorial decision back at the heart of communication.
editorial.p2: This work translates into concrete deliverables: editorial charter, message map, content lines, structured arguments.

strategy.title: Communication that starts from reality
strategy.p1: The proposed communications strategy rests on a simple principle: credibility is built on verifiable facts and honest narratives. Rather than stacking messages, the point is to build a coherent narrative — one the organisation can stand behind.
strategy.p2: Concretely: an audit of existing content, definition of priorities, choice of formats, measurement of reception. A sober approach, driven by clarity.

hero.title: Passing on a standard.
hero.subtitle: The craft is learned in the field — but it is also passed on, through method, example and supervised practice. A pedagogy of experience, drawn from twenty years of professional practice.

philosophy.title: Learn by doing, progress by understanding
philosophy.p1: Knowledge transfer is not the delivery of knowledge but an accompaniment: putting participants in real situations, securing their attempts, debriefing their errors. Workshops rely on real cases and field exercises — never on theory alone.
philosophy.p2: The goal is not to teach recipes but to build reflexes: verify before asserting, listen before questioning, prioritise before writing.
